subject: 🏃 Sunday — 10 mi Long Run + Maurten Gel Rehearsal (Wk 8 Deload)
html:
Tomorrow: 10 mi Long Run — easy aerobic by HR (Z2, 140–150), with the first Maurten Gel 100 rehearsal. The run itself is deload-easy; the real workout is practicing fueling at effort. This is the direct fix for the Presidio problem — one gel in 97 min won't cut it for a 3.5-hour marathon, and tomorrow is where you start rebuilding that skill.

Fueling protocol: 1 Maurten Gel 100 at T−5 (right before you start), then 1 gel every ~25–30 min, targeting ~50–60 g/hr. Add Maurten Drink Mix sips from the handheld between gels. This is the re-introduction week — no pressure to hit 70–80 g/hr yet, just confirm the hydrogel format sits well and you can get gels down while running. Hydration: carry ~16–20 oz water in a vest or second bottle (self-supported, no fountains on the door route), drink to thirst, ~½ LMNT packet in a separate bottle for sodium (~500 mg). Keep carbs and electrolytes in separate vessels — don't mix LMNT into the Maurten Drink Mix.

Pre-run activation (5 min): quadruped hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus the PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

Right hamstring watch. The twinge from Wednesday should be mostly cleared after 4 days. Do a few gentle hamstring sweeps in the warm-up. If it talks during the run, shorten rather than push through — deload week, not the time to test it.

Focus cue: gel timing, not pace. Set a repeating 25-min timer on your watch so you don't have to think about when the next gel is due. Take each one on schedule even if you're not hungry — that's the whole point. The Maurten hydrogel is firmer than PF30 and designed to go down easier at effort; notice the difference.

Where you are: Week 8 of 12, deload — 28 days to race day. Knee has been 1/5 every run since Presidio. The engine and durability are there; the fueling is the project. Tomorrow starts fixing it. Lay out gels, handheld, vest, and LMNT tonight. Bed by 10, alarm for your usual morning slot.
